name: Husqvarna 580BTS Backpack Blower
title: Husqvarna 580BTS Backpack Blower: Specs & Buying Guide
meta: Husqvarna 580BTS backpack blower specs, real-world use on tree and cleanup crews, fit and comfort notes, and what to know before you buy one.
tagline: Big-displacement backpack blower for crews that clean up a lot of ground every day.
summary: The Husqvarna 580BTS is the top of Husqvarna's gas backpack blower line, built for crews that move leaves, sawdust and chip spill across big properties every day. It pairs a 75.6 cc X-Torq engine with a padded harness and a hip-mounted throttle so one person can run it for hours.
highlights: 75.6 cc X-Torq two-stroke engine built for all-day commercial use
Padded, ventilated harness and hip belt to spread the load
Tube-mounted throttle with cruise control
Large air filter suited to dusty jobsite conditions
Strong enough for wet leaves, wood chips and packed debris
specs: Backpack frame with padded harness and hip belt

body.h: Where the 580BTS fits on a tree crew
p: Cleanup is the part of the job the customer actually sees. After the climber is down and the chipper is off, somebody has to get sawdust off the driveway, chips out of the flower beds and twigs out of the lawn before the truck leaves. A handheld blower takes forever on a big lot. The Husqvarna 580BTS is the kind of machine that makes that last half hour a ten-minute job.

It is the largest backpack model in the Husqvarna lineup, and it is aimed at commercial landscape and tree crews rather than homeowners. If you are only blowing off a patio once a week it is overkill. If you have a crew that does several removals and a lot of fall leaf work, the extra air volume pays for itself in time saved.

The 75.6 cc X-Torq engine is the heart of it. X-Torq is Husqvarna's design for lower fuel use and lower emissions compared to an older two-stroke of the same size, which matters when the blower runs most of the day. In use, the 580BTS has enough push to move wet, matted leaves and to roll wood chips off pavement without having to chase every piece.

The throttle sits on the tube, with a cruise setting so you can lock the engine at a steady speed for long passes across a lawn. Run it with fresh 50:1 mix, keep the air filter clean, and replace the spark plug and fuel filter as part of a regular service. Like any big two-stroke, it rewards a few minutes of maintenance each week.

A few habits keep a 580 running well. Let it idle for a few seconds before you go to full throttle, and let it cool down at idle before you shut it off after a long run. Store it with the fuel tank empty or with stabilized fuel over the winter. Most of the starting complaints you hear about big blowers come from fuel that sat in the tank for months.

A blower this size only works if the harness does its job. The 580BTS uses a padded, ventilated back pad with shoulder straps and a hip belt, so most of the weight rides on your hips instead of your shoulders. Take the time to adjust it at the start of the season. A blower that hangs low or swings will wear you out quickly.

Wear hearing protection every time. Backpack blowers are loud at the operator's ear, and eye protection is just as important when you are blowing grit and chips around. Keep bystanders and the homeowner's car out of the blast path.

Buy the Husqvarna 580BTS if you run a commercial crew, cover large properties, or do heavy fall cleanups and want one blower that never feels short of air. If you mostly need a light machine for small yards, a smaller Husqvarna backpack model will be easier to carry and cheaper to buy. Browse the rest of our blowers and other equipment to compare.
If you already run Husqvarna saws, the husqvarna blower 580bts fits right into the same fuel can and service routine, which keeps the truck simple.

faq.q: What engine does the Husqvarna 580BTS use?
faq.a: It uses a 75.6 cc X-Torq two-stroke engine that runs on a 50:1 mix of gasoline and two-stroke oil.

faq.q: Is the 580BTS too much blower for a homeowner?
faq.a: For most homeowners, yes. It is built for commercial crews and large properties. A smaller backpack blower is lighter and less expensive for occasional yard work.

faq.q: How heavy is the Husqvarna 580BTS?
faq.a: It weighs about 25.6 lb dry, which is why the padded harness and hip belt matter. Adjust them so the weight rides on your hips.

faq.q: What maintenance does it need?
faq.a: Use fresh fuel mix, clean or replace the air filter regularly, and replace the spark plug and fuel filter on a regular schedule. Follow the service intervals in the operator's manual.

name: Husqvarna 3120XP Chainsaw (Power Head Only)
title: Husqvarna 3120XP Chainsaw Power Head: Specs & Guide
meta: Husqvarna 3120XP power head specs, bar and chain pairing, and how this 118.8 cc saw handles big wood, slabbing and milling. Read before you buy.
tagline: Husqvarna's biggest saw, for giant trunks, big stump work and chainsaw milling.
summary: The Husqvarna 3120XP is the largest chainsaw Husqvarna makes, a 118.8 cc power head for the biggest wood you will ever face. It is sold as a power head only, so you pick the long bar and chain that suit your work, whether that is bucking huge trunks or running an Alaskan-style mill.
highlights: 118.8 cc engine, Husqvarna's largest chainsaw
Sold as a power head so you choose the bar and chain
Built to pull long bars in big hardwood and for milling
Decompression valve to ease starting
Heavy-duty air filtration for long, dusty cuts
specs: about 22.9 lb (power head, no bar or chain)
3/8 in or .404 in, depending on bar setup
Power head only, bar and chain not included

p: Most tree work never needs a saw this size. A 70 cc or 90 cc saw handles nearly every removal. The Husqvarna 3120 XP is for the jobs where those saws run out of bar or out of power: old-growth trunks, huge oak and sycamore butts, big stumps, and slabbing logs into lumber with a chainsaw mill.

Because it is sold as a power head only, you set it up for your work. Crews that buck big wood usually run a long bar with a full-chisel or semi-chisel chain. Millers often run an even longer bar with a ripping chain. Check Husqvarna's bar recommendations for the saw and match sprocket, pitch and gauge before you order.

That flexibility is also why the 3120XP shows up at sawmills, on storm crews dealing with blown-over giants, and with timber framers who need to square up large beams. It is a specialty saw, but in the right hands it is the only tool that makes some cuts possible.

With 118.8 cc and roughly 8.4 hp, the 3120XP pulls a long bar through dense wood without bogging. That is its real job: keeping chain speed up when there are 36 inches or more of bar buried in a log. It is heavy, at about 22.9 lb before you add a bar and chain, so it is a saw you work from the ground, braced and on good footing.

The decompression valve makes starting a saw this size manageable. Even so, plan your starts on the ground with a firm grip and the chain brake on. On long cuts, let the saw do the work and keep the chain sharp. A dull chain on a saw this big just makes heat and dust.

Run it at full throttle when cutting and do not lug it. Big two-strokes stay healthier when they spin freely. Clean the air filter and cylinder fins often, because long cuts in big wood make a lot of fine dust, and check the sprocket for wear every time you change a chain. On milling setups, watch bar oil closely and consider an auxiliary oiler on very long bars.

Big bars mean big kickback zones. Wear chainsaw protective chaps or pants, a helmet with face and hearing protection, gloves and cut-resistant boots. Know where the bar tip is at all times, and never use a saw this size above shoulder height. Anyone running it should be trained in felling and bucking large wood and follow ANSI Z133 practices on tree jobs.
Large-diameter wood also stores a lot of tension. Read the log, plan your relief cuts, and keep the helpers clear of the roll zone.

body.h: Is it the right saw for you
p: If you regularly cut wood that is wider than a 36-inch bar can handle, or you mill slabs, the 3120XP is worth its price. For general removal work, a Husqvarna 395XP or a 572XP will be lighter and faster on most of the day's cuts.
Think about the rest of the job too. A saw this size needs a truck or a trailer, a way to move huge rounds, and a crew that knows how to roll and wedge big wood safely.

faq.q: Does the Husqvarna 3120XP come with a bar and chain?
faq.a: No. This listing is the power head only. You choose a bar and chain that match the saw's sprocket and your work, such as bucking big logs or milling.

faq.q: What is the displacement of the 3120XP?
faq.a: It is 118.8 cc, which makes it the largest chainsaw Husqvarna builds.

faq.q: Is the 3120XP good for chainsaw milling?
faq.a: Yes. Its power makes it a common choice for chainsaw mills running long bars. Use a ripping chain and keep it sharp for the best results.

faq.q: How much does the 3120XP weigh?
faq.a: About 22.9 lb for the power head alone. A long bar and chain add several more pounds.

name: Husqvarna 372XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 372XP Chainsaw: Specs, Bars & Buying Guide
meta: Husqvarna 372XP chainsaw specs, bar lengths, how it runs on removals and firewood, and how it compares with the newer 572XP. Read before you buy.
tagline: The classic 70 cc pro saw for removals, bucking and storm cleanup.
summary: The Husqvarna 372XP is the 70 cc pro chainsaw that a generation of tree crews and loggers learned on, known for its strong torque and simple, durable build. It runs bars from 18 to 28 inches and handles everything from removals to bucking firewood-length rounds.
highlights: 70.7 cc engine with strong low-end torque
Runs 18 to 28 in bars for removals and bucking
Simple, proven design that many shops know how to service
Good power-to-weight for a 70 cc class saw
Shares many parts and accessories with other Husqvarna pro saws

p: Ask any veteran climber or logger about the chainsaw Husqvarna 372XP and you will hear the same thing: it is a workhorse. It has the grunt to pull a 24-inch bar through hardwood, it is light enough to carry all day on the ground, and it is simple to work on. That combination made it one of the most common pro saws on tree trucks for years.

Husqvarna has since moved its main 70 cc pro offering to the 572XP with AutoTune, and 372XP availability varies by market and dealer. Many crews still run 372XPs, and parts remain easy to find, which is part of why the 372xp keeps coming up in searches.

There is a reason used 372XPs still sell quickly. The engine is easy to rebuild, the clutch and sprocket are simple, and the saw tolerates hard use. Many climbers bought one as their first serious saw and kept it running for a decade or more with nothing more than regular filters, plugs and chains.

On a removal, the 372XP is the ground saw. It bucks wood as it comes down, cuts the trunk into manageable rounds and drops small to medium spars. A 20 or 24-inch bar suits most tree work. Firewood and storm crews often go to 24 or 28 inches. Keep in mind the saw's sweet spot is the middle of that range; longer bars work but slow the chain in big hardwood.
Fuel it with fresh 50:1 mix and keep the air filter clean, especially when cutting dry, dusty wood. Sharpen the chain often and check the sprocket and bar rails when you change chains.

For storm work, a 372XP with a 24-inch bar is a very practical setup. It has enough reach for most blowdowns, it is light enough to carry over brush and debris, and it has the power to cut through the root plate and trunk of medium trees. Swap to a shorter bar for limbing if you run it all day, since a shorter bar is quicker and less tiring.

The 572XP is the modern replacement in the 70 cc class. It adds AutoTune, which adjusts the carburetor for fuel, altitude and air filter condition, and a slightly different power curve. The 372XP is manually tuned and has a simpler design that some mechanics prefer. If you are buying new, compare the two side by side. See our Husqvarna 572XP page for the details.

Both saws use the same 3/8 in pitch chains and many of the same bars, so your existing bars and chains will often carry over if you move from one to the other. Confirm the bar mount and drive link count before you order.

Wear chainsaw chaps or pants, a helmet with face and hearing protection, gloves and cut-resistant boots. Check the chain brake before every shift. On tree jobs, follow ANSI Z133 and the operator's manual, and only run the saw if you are trained for the cuts you are making.

faq.q: What bar length is best on a Husqvarna 372XP?
faq.a: A 20 or 24 in bar suits most tree and firewood work. The saw runs bars from 18 to 28 in, but it is fastest in the middle of that range.

faq.q: Is the 372XP still made?
faq.a: Husqvarna's current 70 cc pro saw is the 572XP, and 372XP availability varies by market. Parts for the 372XP remain widely available.

faq.q: What fuel mix does the 372XP use?
faq.a: It runs on a 50:1 mix of unleaded gasoline and quality two-stroke oil. Use fresh fuel or a pre-mixed fuel for best results.

name: Husqvarna 395XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 395XP Chainsaw: Specs & Buying Guide
meta: Husqvarna 395XP chainsaw specs, best bar lengths, and how this 93.6 cc saw performs on big removals, storm work and large hardwood. Read before buying.
tagline: A 90 cc class saw for big removals, large hardwood and storm work.
summary: The Husqvarna 395XP is a 93.6 cc pro chainsaw built for big wood, from large removals to storm cleanup on oversized trunks. It has the torque to pull long bars in dense hardwood while staying simple and durable enough for daily crew use.
highlights: 93.6 cc engine with heavy torque for long bars
Built for large-diameter removals and storm work
Decompression valve for easier starting
Durable design with a long service record
A step up from the 70 cc class without the bulk of the 3120XP

body.h: When you need a 90 cc saw
p: Most crews carry a 50 cc saw for limbing and a 70 cc saw for bucking. The Husqvarna 395 XP comes off the truck when the wood gets big: a 40-inch oak butt, a storm-split sycamore, a stump that has to come down to grade. With 93.6 cc and around 6.6 hp, the 395xp keeps a long bar moving where a 70 cc saw starts to bog.

It is a big saw, so it is a ground saw. You will not carry it far into the woods all day, and you should not. Park it near the work, bring it in for the big cuts, and let the smaller saw handle the rest.

Storm crews especially value a saw like this. After a big wind event, the work is often huge trees across roads and houses, and the ability to make a single clean cut through a large trunk saves time and reduces risk. A smaller saw forces you into multiple cuts from both sides, which takes longer and can put you in awkward positions.

The 395XP is commonly run with bars from 24 to 36 inches. A 28 or 32-inch bar is a good all-round choice for big removal work. Use a 3/8 in pitch chain that matches your bar and sprocket, and keep spare loops sharp and ready. On big hardwood, a sharp chain makes more difference than any other factor.
Check bar oil output when you install a long bar, and keep the oil tank topped. Long bars use more oil, and a dry bar wears out fast.

If you cut a lot of dirty wood, such as storm debris with grit in the bark, carry a spare chain or two. A big saw on a long bar dulls quickly in dirty wood, and swapping a chain is faster than filing a badly dulled one in the field. Keep a bar tool, a file kit and spare plugs in the saw box.

The chainsaw Husqvarna 395xp has a reputation for lasting. It is a manually tuned saw with a straightforward design, which makes it easy for a shop to keep running. Keep the air filter clean, use fresh 50:1 fuel, and replace the spark plug and fuel filter on schedule. Inspect the anti-vibration mounts and the chain brake regularly.
When the saw starts to feel weak, look at the simple things first: the chain, the air filter, the spark plug and the fuel. A fresh plug and filter fix a surprising number of problems.

A long bar on a big saw has a large kickback zone and a lot of chain speed. Wear chaps or chainsaw pants, a helmet with face screen and hearing protection, gloves and cut-resistant boots. Plan cuts on large wood carefully, watch for tension and compression, and keep the ground crew out of the roll zone. Follow ANSI Z133 on tree jobs, and make sure every operator is trained. If you need even more saw, look at the Husqvarna 3120XP.

faq.q: What is the displacement of the Husqvarna 395XP?
faq.a: The 395XP has a 93.6 cc engine producing about 6.6 hp.

faq.q: What bar length should I run on a 395XP?
faq.a: Bars from 24 to 36 in are common. A 28 or 32 in bar suits most big removal work.

faq.q: Is the 395XP too big for everyday tree work?
faq.a: For limbing and most bucking, yes. It is best as the big-wood saw on the truck, alongside a 50 cc and 70 cc saw.

faq.q: How heavy is the 395XP?
faq.a: About 17.4 lb for the power head, before the bar and chain.

name: Husqvarna 450 Rancher Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 450 Rancher Chainsaw: Specs & Buying Guide
meta: Husqvarna 450 Rancher chainsaw specs, bar sizes, real use on firewood and storm cleanup, and how it compares with pro saws. Read before you buy one.
tagline: A 50 cc all-round saw for firewood, storm cleanup and property work.
summary: The Husqvarna 450 Rancher is a 50.2 cc all-round chainsaw for landowners, farmers and part-time cutters who need more than a homeowner saw. It runs an 18 or 20-inch bar and handles firewood, storm cleanup and small felling without the price of a pro model.
highlights: 50.2 cc X-Torq engine for firewood and property work
Commonly sold with an 18 or 20 in bar
Smart Start and air purge for easier starting
Air Injection pre-cleaning to extend air filter life
Good value step up from homeowner saws

p: The Husqvarna 450 Rancher chainsaw sits between homeowner saws and the pro XP line. It is built for people who cut regularly but not every day: landowners clearing fence lines, farmers keeping up with blowdowns, and anyone who heats with wood. If that sounds like you, the Husqvarna 450 gives you enough power to cut firewood all afternoon without the cost of a pro saw.
Tree crews usually run lighter, faster pro saws for daily work, but a Rancher 450 is a common pick for a second saw on the farm truck or for storm cleanup at home.

It is also a good choice for someone who wants a saw that will grow with them. The 50 cc size handles most property tasks, and the husqvarna rancher 450 is easy to find parts for at almost any dealer.

The 50.2 cc X-Torq engine pulls an 18 or 20-inch bar well in softwood and medium hardwood. Bucking 12 to 16-inch logs into firewood rounds is its sweet spot. It will cut bigger wood, but it takes patience, and that is where a 60 or 70 cc saw earns its price.

Starting is easy for a saw this size thanks to Smart Start and an air purge primer. Keep a sharp chain, clean the air filter often, and use fresh fuel. Most starting and running problems with Rancher saws trace back to old fuel or a clogged filter.

Match chain to bar. Most 450 Rancher saws run 0.325 in pitch chain. Count the drive links or check the stamp on the bar before ordering a replacement. A spare sharp chain in the truck turns a slow afternoon into a quick one. Keep the chain tension snug but not tight, and check it after the first few cuts on a new chain, since new chains stretch.

Compared to the Husqvarna 550XP Mark II, the 450 Rancher is heavier for its power and has a more basic build. The 550XP revs higher, cuts faster and is built for daily professional use. If you cut a few weekends a year, the Rancher is the better value. If you cut for a living, buy the pro saw.

Wear chaps, eye and hearing protection, gloves and sturdy boots, and use the chain brake when you walk with the saw. Learn safe felling and bucking before you take on leaning or storm-damaged trees. Trees under tension from storms are some of the most dangerous wood to cut. When in doubt, call a trained tree crew.
Before each use, check the chain brake, the chain catcher and the throttle lockout. These safety features only help if they work.

faq.q: What bar comes on the Husqvarna 450 Rancher?
faq.a: It is usually sold with an 18 or 20 in bar. A 20 in bar is a popular choice for firewood.

faq.q: Is the 450 Rancher a professional saw?
faq.a: It is a heavy-duty saw for regular use, but it is not part of Husqvarna's XP pro line. Daily professional users usually choose an XP model.

faq.q: What is the displacement of the Husqvarna 450?
faq.a: The 450 Rancher has a 50.2 cc engine rated at about 3.2 hp.

faq.q: What fuel does the 450 Rancher use?
faq.a: A 50:1 mix of unleaded gasoline and two-stroke oil. Fresh or pre-mixed fuel helps it start and run well.

name: Husqvarna 525PT5S Gas Pole Saw
title: Husqvarna Pole Saw 525PT5S: Gas Telescoping Specs
meta: Husqvarna pole saw 525PT5S: telescoping gas pole saw for pruning from the ground. Specs, reach, real crew use and safety tips before you buy.
tagline: Telescoping gas pole saw for pruning and clearance work from the ground.
summary: The Husqvarna pole saw 525PT5S is a professional gas pole saw with a telescoping shaft, built for pruning and clearance work from the ground. A 25.4 cc X-Torq engine drives a 12-inch bar at the end of the shaft, so you can take limbs over driveways and roofs without a ladder.
highlights: 25.4 cc X-Torq engine
Telescoping shaft for extra reach
12 in bar and chain at the cutting head
Harness-ready for long sessions
Pro-grade build for daily clearance and pruning

body.h: What a gas pole saw does for a crew
p: A lot of tree work is not climbing at all. It is raising canopies over driveways, clearing limbs off roofs, and opening up sight lines along roads and fences. A good gas chainsaw on a pole lets one person do that work from the ground, quickly and without a ladder. The Husqvarna 525PT5S is Husqvarna's professional pole saw for that job.

The telescoping shaft is the key feature. You can collapse it to work low limbs or to load it on the truck, then extend it for high cuts. That means one tool covers a wide range of heights instead of carrying two fixed-length saws.

For crews, the husqvarna gas pole saw is a quick way to finish up pruning after a climber comes down, or to take small deadwood without setting a line. For property managers and municipal crews, it handles clearance pruning over sidewalks and roads all day.

The 25.4 cc X-Torq engine sits at the bottom of the shaft, where it balances the weight of the cutting head. It drives a 12-inch bar and chain through the shaft. For pruning cuts up to a few inches thick, that is plenty. On bigger limbs, make a small undercut first so the bark does not tear, and let the saw cut at its own speed.

Keep the chain sharp, check the bar oil level every time you refuel, and grease the cutting head per the manual. A dry gearbox or a dull chain will make the saw feel weak long before the engine is the problem.

Never use a pole saw near power lines. Keep at least the minimum approach distance required by OSHA and ANSI Z133, and assume all lines are energized. Only qualified line-clearance workers should work near electrical conductors.

Stand to the side of the limb, not under it, and wear a helmet, eye protection, hearing protection and gloves. Watch for limbs that can bounce off the shaft or swing back toward you. Use the harness for long sessions to save your back and keep better control.

Take frequent breaks on long pruning days. Holding a pole saw overhead is tiring work, and fatigue is when mistakes happen. Clear the drop zone before every cut and let helpers know where limbs will fall.

body.h: Is it the right pole saw
p: If you do regular pruning or clearance work and want a gas pole saw that holds up to daily use, the 525PT5S is a strong choice. For occasional homeowner use, a lighter or battery pole saw may be easier. For cuts out of reach of any pole, you will need a climber or a bucket. Compare more options in our chainsaws section.

faq.q: What engine does the Husqvarna 525PT5S use?
faq.a: It uses a 25.4 cc X-Torq two-stroke engine running on 50:1 fuel mix.

faq.q: What bar length is on the 525PT5S?
faq.a: It has a 12 in bar and chain at the cutting head.

faq.q: Can I use a pole saw near power lines?
faq.a: No. Keep well clear of power lines. Only qualified line-clearance arborists may work near energized conductors, and they follow strict approach distances.

faq.q: Does the shaft telescope?
faq.a: Yes. The telescoping shaft lets you collapse it for low cuts and transport and extend it for higher limbs.

name: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II Chainsaw: Specs & Guide
meta: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II specs, bar sizes and how this 50 cc AutoTune pro saw handles limbing, bucking and small removals. Read this before you buy.
tagline: A light, fast 50 cc pro saw for limbing, bucking and small removals.
summary: The Husqvarna 550XP Mark II is a 50.1 cc professional chainsaw that many tree crews use as their everyday ground saw for limbing, bucking and small removals. It is light, revs fast, and uses AutoTune to keep the carburetor set correctly as conditions change.
highlights: 50.1 cc engine with a high-revving, fast-cutting feel
AutoTune adjusts the carburetor automatically
Light power head for long days of limbing and brush work
Runs bars from about 13 to 20 in
Durable Mark II updates over the original 550XP

p: On most tree jobs, the saw that runs the most hours is not the biggest one. It is the 50 cc saw that limbs out the brush, cuts small wood for the chipper and bucks the rounds the bigger saw left behind. The Husqvarna 550 XP Mark II is built for exactly that work. It is light enough to carry around the job all day, and it revs fast enough that small cuts take a second or two.

Many climbers also choose the husqvarna 550xp chainsaw as the saw they send up on a line for bigger cuts aloft, where a top-handle saw runs out of bar. It handles well, balances nicely and does not wear you out.

On brush-heavy jobs it is often the saw that never gets turned off. One person feeds the chipper while another works through the piles with the 550, cutting long limbs down to lengths that feed cleanly. Light weight matters most in that role.

The Mark II version updated the original 550XP with improvements aimed at durability and reliability in daily professional use. It keeps the features that made the first one popular: a compact power head, a fast chain speed and AutoTune.

AutoTune is Husqvarna's system for adjusting the carburetor automatically. It compensates for fuel quality, altitude, temperature and the condition of the air filter, so the saw stays close to its best tune without you reaching for a screwdriver. That is useful on crews where several people share saws and nobody wants to spend time tuning.

The 550XP runs bars from about 13 to 20 inches. A 16-inch bar is the most popular choice for limbing and brush work because it is quick and light. An 18 or 20-inch bar adds reach for bucking and small felling. Use 0.325 in pitch chain that matches the gauge and drive link count stamped on your bar.

Keep it sharp. A high-revving saw like the 550XP really shows the difference between a fresh chain and a tired one. Touch up the cutters at every fuel stop and the saw will keep cutting fast all day. Clean the air filter regularly and replace the spark plug and fuel filter on schedule.

body.h: Who should buy it and safety
p: Buy the 550XP Mark II if you need a reliable, light, pro-grade saw for daily limbing, bucking and small removals. For heavier bucking or big wood, pair it with a 70 cc saw such as the Husqvarna 572XP. If you want a saw for occasional property work, the 450 Rancher is less expensive.

Wear chainsaw chaps or pants, a helmet with face and hearing protection, gloves and cut-resistant boots. Use the chain brake when moving between cuts. If you send this saw aloft, use a proper saw lanyard and follow ANSI Z133 and your employer's rules for rear-handle saw use in the tree. Only trained operators should run a chainsaw at height.

faq.q: What is the displacement of the Husqvarna 550XP?
faq.a: The 550XP Mark II has a 50.1 cc engine producing about 4.0 hp.

faq.q: What bar length is best on a 550XP?
faq.a: A 16 in bar is the most popular for limbing and brush. An 18 or 20 in bar adds reach for bucking and small felling.

faq.q: What is AutoTune?
faq.a: AutoTune is Husqvarna's automatic carburetor adjustment. It compensates for fuel, altitude, temperature and air filter condition so the saw stays well tuned.

faq.q: Is the 550XP good for a beginner?
faq.a: It is easy to handle, but it is a fast professional saw. New users should get proper training and start with simple ground cuts.

name: Husqvarna 572XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 572XP Chainsaw: Specs, Bars & Buying Guide
meta: Husqvarna 572XP specs, bar lengths and real use on removals, bucking and storm work, plus how it compares with the older 372XP. Read before you buy.
tagline: Husqvarna's modern 70 cc pro saw for removals, bucking and storm cleanup.
summary: The Husqvarna 572XP is Husqvarna's 70 cc class professional chainsaw, the modern successor to the 372XP and a go-to bucking saw on tree crews. It pairs a 70.6 cc engine with AutoTune and runs bars from 18 to 28 inches for removals, storm work and firewood.
highlights: 70.6 cc engine built for heavy bucking and felling
AutoTune keeps the carburetor adjusted
Runs 18 to 28 in bars
Strong torque in big hardwood
Modern replacement for the 372XP

body.h: The 70 cc saw on the truck
p: Every removal crew needs a saw that bridges the gap between the light limbing saw and the big-wood saw. That is the 70 cc class, and the Husqvarna 572 XP is Husqvarna's current pro model in it. It drops spars, bucks trunks into rounds the loader can handle and cuts through storm-damaged wood without fuss.

With about 5.8 hp from a 70.6 cc engine, the 572xp has noticeably more power than the 372XP it replaced, and it keeps that power on longer bars. Crews that run 24-inch bars most of the day will feel the difference in dense hardwood.

It is also a solid felling saw for small and medium trees on the ground. A 70 cc saw has enough bar for most trunks you will fell whole, and enough power to keep the back cut moving while you set wedges.

Like any pro saw, the 572XP still needs the basics. Use fresh 50:1 fuel, clean the air filter often, keep the cylinder fins clear and replace the spark plug and fuel filter on schedule. Most problems with modern pro saws come from old fuel or neglected filters, not the engine.

Let the saw warm up for a few seconds before cutting, especially on cold mornings, and let AutoTune settle after a fuel change or a filter cleaning. If the saw ever runs poorly after a filter change, a few minutes of normal cutting usually lets it adjust.

The 572XP runs bars from 18 to 28 inches with 3/8 in pitch chain. A 20-inch bar is quick and handy for removals. A 24-inch bar is a popular all-round choice. Search interest in husqvarna 572xp specs is high for a reason: people want to know whether it is worth the upgrade. For most crews running a 70 cc saw daily, the answer is yes, especially if the old saw is due for a rebuild.

body.h: What the T435 is built for
p: A top-handle saw is a climber's tool. It is short, light and balanced so you can hold it in a working position while you are tied in. The Husqvarna T435 is a 35 cc version of that idea, with a little more power than the smallest climbing saws and a modest price.

In the tree, the t435 husqvarna saw handles pruning cuts, deadwood and limbing on removals. With a 12 or 14-inch bar, it takes limbs up to medium size comfortably. For bigger wood aloft, most climbers send up a rear-handle saw on a line.

The husqvarna t435 chainsaw is a common choice for newer climbers, smaller tree services and anyone who wants a dependable gas top-handle saw without paying for the top pro model. It also suits experienced climbers who want a backup saw on the truck.

The 35.2 cc X-Torq engine provides steady power and reasonable fuel use. On a top-handle saw, power is always a trade-off with weight. The T435 sits in the middle: stronger than a 25 cc saw, but still light enough to hang off your saddle all day.

Keep the chain sharp and the bar oiled. A top-handle saw cutting with a dull chain forces you to push harder, and pushing is what gets climbers into bad positions. A sharp chain lets you make clean, controlled cuts with little effort.

Carry it on a saw lanyard clipped to the side of your saddle, and keep the chain brake on whenever you are moving or repositioning. Start it with the chain brake engaged, using a method approved in the operator's manual and by your training.

Top-handle chainsaws are designed for trained arborists working aloft. ANSI Z133 sets rules for their use, and the manufacturer's instructions say how to hold and start them. Use two hands whenever possible, keep the saw tied to your saddle with a proper saw lanyard, and start it in a safe position. Never use a top-handle saw on the ground as a general-purpose saw. A rear-handle saw is safer for ground work.

Wear a helmet with eye and hearing protection, gloves and appropriate leg protection as your employer requires. Be aware of where your lanyard and climbing line are in relation to the bar at all times. Get training before you take a top-handle saw up a tree.

Basic maintenance keeps the T435 running reliably. Clean the air filter often, use fresh fuel and replace the spark plug and fuel filter regularly. We carry a replacement fuel filter for the T435 so you can keep a spare in the saw box.
If you need a lighter saw or more power, compare the Husqvarna T540XP Mark III, the pro top-handle saw in Husqvarna's lineup.
Keep spare chains sharp and ready. Small saws dull quickly in dirty bark and deadwood, and a fresh chain is the fastest way to restore cutting speed in the tree.

As an arborist chainsaw, the T525 shines on pruning jobs, utility clearance trims and fine work in ornamental trees. Many climbers carry it alongside a good pruning hand saw so they can switch between powered cuts and fine handsaw cuts without changing position.

h1: Husqvarna Chainsaw Fuel Filter for the T435

tagline: Replacement in-tank fuel filter for the Husqvarna T435 top-handle saw.
summary: This Husqvarna chainsaw fuel filter is the in-tank replacement filter for the T435 top-handle saw. It keeps dirt and debris in the tank from reaching the carburetor, and it is one of the cheapest ways to keep a climbing saw starting and running well.
highlights: Replacement in-tank fuel filter for the Husqvarna T435
Keeps debris out of the carburetor
Inexpensive part worth keeping in the saw box
Simple to swap with a hooked wire or fuel line tool
Part of a regular tune-up with a new plug and air filter
specs: Inside the fuel tank on the end of the fuel line
Replace at least once a season or per manual

p: Every chainsaw has a small filter on the end of the fuel line, sitting in the bottom of the tank. Its job is simple: stop dirt, sawdust and bits of debris from getting sucked into the carburetor. On a top-handle saw like the T435, which gets refueled on the ground, in the bucket and sometimes in less than tidy conditions, that filter works hard.

When the filter gets clogged, the engine starves for fuel. The saw may start and idle fine, then bog or die when you hit the throttle. It may run for a minute and quit, or lose power in the middle of a cut. Those symptoms often get blamed on the carburetor, when a ten-dollar filter is the real problem.

Husqvarna's operator manual gives service intervals, and replacing the fuel filter at least once a season is a good habit for most users. Climbers who run the saw every day may want to change it more often. Replace it any time you see the saw starving for fuel, after running a tank of dirty or old fuel, or when you service the saw after storage.
It is also smart to keep a spare in the saw box. A fuel filter weighs almost nothing and can save a day's work if a saw starts acting up on a job far from the shop.

A fuel filter for Husqvarna saws is model-specific in some cases, so order the one listed for your saw rather than a universal part when you can. A filter that does not fit the fuel line snugly can slip off in the tank, and then you are pulling the line back out on the tailgate.

With the saw cool and on a clean surface, drain the tank and remove the fuel cap. Use a hooked wire or a small fuel line tool to fish the fuel line out of the tank, being careful not to stretch or tear the line. Pull the old filter off the end of the line, push the new one on firmly and drop it back into the tank so it sits at the bottom.
While you are in there, look at the fuel line. If it is hard, cracked or swollen, replace it too. A cracked fuel line will let air in and cause the same running problems as a clogged filter.

Most fuel filter problems start with the fuel itself. Mix fresh fuel in a clean can, use quality two-stroke oil, and do not leave mixed fuel sitting for months. Pre-mixed fuel is a good option for saws that sit between jobs. Keep the area around the fuel cap clean before you open it so sawdust does not fall into the tank.
Pair a new filter with a fresh spark plug and a clean air filter for a full tune-up. See the Husqvarna T435 page for more on the saw, or browse more chainsaw parts.

faq.q: How do I know if my chainsaw fuel filter is clogged?
faq.a: Common signs are a saw that bogs or dies under throttle, loses power in the cut or will not stay running after starting. Replacing the filter is a quick, low-cost first check.

faq.q: Does this filter fit other Husqvarna saws?
faq.a: This listing is for the T435. Fuel filters differ between models, so check your operator's manual or parts list before ordering for another saw.

faq.q: How often should I replace the fuel filter?
faq.a: At least once a season for most users, or more often for saws that run every day. Follow the interval in your manual.

name: NGK BPMR7A Spark Plug
title: NGK BPMR7A Spark Plug: Specs, Fitment & Tips
meta: NGK BPMR7A spark plug for chainsaws and small engines. Thread and hex size, what the code means, gap and fitment tips, and when to replace it.
tagline: A common resistor spark plug for chainsaws and small two-stroke engines.
summary: The NGK BPMR7A is one of the most common spark plugs in chainsaws and small outdoor power equipment, a 14 mm resistor plug with a projected tip. If your saw, blower or trimmer calls for a BPMR7A spark plug, keeping a couple in the truck is cheap insurance against hard starting.
highlights: 14 mm thread, 13/16 in (20.8 mm) hex
Resistor type to reduce electrical interference
Projected insulator tip
Heat range 7 in NGK's numbering
Widely used in chainsaws, blowers and small engines

p: NGK spark plug codes look cryptic, but they tell you a lot. In the bpmr7a, the B means a 14 mm thread with a 13/16 in hex. P means a projected insulator tip. M marks a compact plug design with a short reach. R means it has a built-in resistor. The 7 is the heat range, and the A is a design variation.

The resistor matters on modern equipment. It cuts down on electrical noise from the ignition, which can affect electronic ignition modules and other electronics. If your manual calls for the resistor version, use it. The ngk bpm7a spark plug is the non-resistor version of the same basic plug, so do not swap them unless your manual allows it.

The BPMR7A is found in a wide range of chainsaws, blowers, trimmers and other small two-stroke engines from several manufacturers. That is part of why the ngk bpmr7a spark plug is such a common search: lots of people own something that uses it.

Do not guess on fitment. Check the operator's manual or the plug that came out of the engine. Heat range, reach and thread all matter. A plug with the wrong reach can hit the piston or leave threads exposed to carbon, and the wrong heat range can cause fouling or overheating.

Set the gap to the figure in your engine's manual using a wire gauge, and do not assume the gap out of the box is correct for your engine. Thread the plug in by hand first to avoid cross-threading, then snug it with a plug wrench. Do not over-tighten, especially in aluminum cylinder heads.

Replace the plug on the schedule in your manual or any time it looks worn, fouled or oily. A black, sooty plug can point to a rich mixture or a dirty air filter. A white, blistered plug can point to a lean condition that needs attention before it damages the engine. Always replace a plug with the engine cool and the plug wire or boot removed, and never test for spark by holding the plug near the open spark plug hole. Fuel vapor can ignite.

A spark plug is the cheapest part in the saw box and one of the first things to check when a saw will not start. Many crews keep a few bpmr7a spark plugs with the files and spare chains. Pair a fresh plug with a new fuel filter and a clean air filter for a quick tune-up, or browse more power equipment parts.

Store spare plugs in their packaging so the electrodes do not get bent or the gap knocked out of spec while rattling around in a tool bag. Check the gap again before installing a plug that has been carried around for a while.

faq.q: What is the difference between the BPMR7A and BPM7A?
faq.a: The R in BPMR7A means it has a built-in resistor. The BPM7A is the non-resistor version. Use the one your engine's manual specifies.

faq.q: What gap should a BPMR7A have?
faq.a: Use the gap listed in your engine's operator manual. Check it with a wire gauge before installing.

faq.q: What thread size is the NGK BPMR7A?
faq.a: It has a 14 mm thread and a 13/16 in (20.8 mm) hex.

faq.q: How often should I replace it?
faq.a: Follow your manual's interval, and replace it any time it is fouled, worn or the engine is hard to start.

name: NGK CMR6H Spark Plug
title: NGK CMR6H Spark Plug: Specs, Fitment & Cross Ref
meta: NGK CMR6H spark plug for small handheld engines. Thread and hex size, what the code means, cross reference tips and how to install it the right way.
tagline: A compact 10 mm resistor plug for small handheld power equipment.
summary: The NGK CMR6H spark plug is a compact 10 mm resistor plug used in many small handheld engines, including trimmers, blowers, pole saws and small chainsaws. Its small size suits the tight cylinder heads of lightweight engines.
highlights: Compact 10 mm thread with a 5/8 in (16 mm) hex
1/2 in (12.7 mm) reach
Resistor type
Heat range 6 in NGK's numbering
Common in small handheld two- and four-stroke engines

p: The cmr6h is part of NGK's compact plug family. The C means a 10 mm thread with a 16 mm hex. M marks the compact design. R means it has a resistor. The 6 is the heat range, and H indicates a 1/2 in (12.7 mm) thread reach.

Compact plugs like the ngk cmr6h are made for small engines where there is not much room in the cylinder head. They are common on trimmers, blowers, edgers, pole saws and small chainsaws. Some small four-stroke handheld engines use them as well.

Always check your operator's manual or the plug you are replacing. Thread, reach and heat range all need to match. The CMR6H and the CMR7H look identical but have different heat ranges. In NGK's system a higher number is a colder plug, so they are not interchangeable unless your manual lists both.

Searches for cmr6h cross reference usually come from people trying to match a plug from another brand. Cross-reference charts are a starting point, but heat ranges do not always line up perfectly between brands. When in doubt, use the plug the engine maker specifies.

If you run several small machines, label which ones use which plug. Crews often run trimmers, blowers and pole saws from different makers, and the plugs look alike. A small chart taped inside the parts bin saves mistakes.

Small plugs strip threads easily, and many small engines have aluminum heads. Thread the cmr6h spark plug in by hand first. If it does not turn smoothly, back it out and start again. Snug it with the correct 5/8 in plug wrench, following the torque guidance in your manual, and do not over-tighten.

Check the gap with a wire gauge against your manual before installing. Make sure the plug boot snaps fully onto the terminal. A loose boot causes misfires that feel like a fuel problem. Always replace a plug with the engine cool and the plug wire or boot removed, and never test for spark by holding the plug near the open spark plug hole. Fuel vapor can ignite.

body.h: Signs it is time for a new plug
p: Hard starting, rough idle, misfires and loss of power are all signs to check the plug. Look at the tip: heavy carbon, oil fouling or a worn electrode all mean it is time to replace it. Because small engines are sensitive, a fresh plug often makes a bigger difference than you would expect.
Plugs are cheap, so keep a few on hand. If your engine calls for the colder version, see the NGK CMR7H, or browse more power equipment parts.
Keep spares in their packaging so the gap stays set and the electrode is protected until you need it.

faq.q: What is the thread size of the NGK CMR6H?
faq.a: It has a 10 mm thread, a 5/8 in (16 mm) hex and a 1/2 in (12.7 mm) reach.

faq.q: Can I use a CMR7H instead of a CMR6H?
faq.a: Only if your engine's manual lists it. The CMR7H is a colder heat range, so it is not a direct swap in every engine.

faq.q: Is there a cmr6h cross reference for other brands?
faq.a: Other brands make similar plugs, but heat ranges do not always match exactly. Use the plug listed in your manual whenever possible.

tagline: In-tank replacement fuel filter to keep debris out of your saw's carburetor.
summary: A chainsaw fuel filter sits on the end of the fuel line inside the tank and keeps debris away from the carburetor. This replacement filter is an easy, low-cost part that solves many bogging and stalling problems before they turn into a carburetor rebuild.
highlights: In-tank fuel pickup filter
Keeps sawdust and grit out of the carburetor
Low-cost tune-up part
Check fitment against your fuel line size
Worth keeping a spare in the saw box
specs: Match to your saw's fuel line and manual
Push-on to the end of the fuel line
Replace at least once a season

p: Every gas chainsaw pulls fuel through a small filter sitting at the bottom of the tank. Sawdust, grit and bits of debris that get into the tank end up there instead of in the carburetor's tiny passages. Over time, that filter loads up and starts to restrict fuel flow.

A restricted filter is one of the most common reasons a saw runs well at idle but bogs or dies at full throttle. It can also cause a saw to lose power partway through a cut or to stall after a few minutes of work. Before you pull the carburetor apart, put in a new chainsaw fuel filter. It is cheap and often fixes the problem.

On a busy crew, where saws are refueled in the back of the truck, on the ground or out of a dusty fuel can, filters clog faster than most people expect. Treat the filter as a regular wear part, not something you only think about when the saw quits.

Chainsaw fuel filters come in different sizes, with different barb sizes for different fuel line diameters. Check your operator's manual or parts list, or compare with the filter you are removing. The filter should push firmly onto the fuel line and stay put. A loose fit can let unfiltered fuel bypass it or let the filter fall off in the tank.
If you run Husqvarna saws, check whether a model-specific filter is listed. For the T435 top-handle saw, we carry a Husqvarna fuel filter for the T435.

Work on a cool saw in a clean area. Drain the tank, then use a hooked wire or fuel line tool to pull the line and filter out through the filler opening. Slide the old filter off, push the new one on firmly and drop it back so it rests at the bottom of the tank where it can pick up fuel at any angle.
Inspect the fuel line while you are there. If it is stiff, cracked or swollen, replace it. A damaged line can let air into the fuel system and cause the same problems as a clogged filter.
Once the new filter is in, refill with fresh fuel, prime the saw if it has a primer and run it through a few full-throttle cuts to make sure it pulls fuel well at all angles.

Keep fuel clean and fresh. Mix in a clean can, use good two-stroke oil and avoid leaving mixed fuel sitting for months. Wipe sawdust away from the fuel cap before opening it. If a saw is going to sit for a while, run it dry or use a stabilized or pre-mixed fuel. Combine a new filter with a fresh spark plug and a clean air filter as part of a regular tune-up, and browse more chainsaw parts to complete the job.

faq.q: How often should I change a chainsaw fuel filter?
faq.a: At least once a season for most users, and more often for saws that run daily or in dirty conditions.

faq.q: Will this filter fit my saw?
faq.a: Fuel filters vary by model and fuel line size. Compare it with your old filter or check your operator's manual before ordering.

faq.q: What are the signs of a clogged fuel filter?
faq.a: Bogging or stalling at full throttle, loss of power in the cut and a saw that will not stay running are common signs.

name: Greenteeth 700 Series Pocket (Straight)
title: Greenteeth 700 Series Pocket, Straight

Replace worn or damaged pockets to keep the wheel balanced

p: In a pocket-style stump grinder system, the pocket bolts to the cutter wheel and the tooth sits in the pocket. The pocket takes much of the shock and abrasion from the stump and the dirt around it. On a wheel set up with the greenteeth 700 series, straight pockets are used in specific positions in the cutting pattern, alongside left and right pockets.

Over time, pockets wear from rocks, dirt and the impact of grinding. A worn pocket may not hold the tooth tight, which can let the tooth shift or break. Replacing damaged pockets keeps the teeth secure and the wheel running true.
Keeping spare pockets on the truck means a damaged pocket does not end a grinding day early. Rocks and buried metal can crack a pocket without warning.

Follow your grinder's tooth pattern and the manufacturer's instructions when you replace a pocket, and use the correct hardware torqued to spec. Replace pockets in the same position and orientation as the originals. Check all teeth and bolts at the same time. Always lock out the grinder and let the wheel stop completely before working on it, and wear gloves and eye protection. Browse more stump grinding teeth and parts.

faq.q: What is a straight pocket for?
faq.a: Straight pockets hold teeth in specific positions in the cutter wheel pattern, working alongside left and right pockets. Follow your wheel's pattern when replacing them.

faq.q: Does this fit other Greenteeth series?
faq.a: This pocket is for the 700 Series system. Other series use different pockets and teeth.

name: Green Teeth Allen Head Bolt
title: Green Teeth Allen Head Bolt for Stump Grinder Teeth
meta: Green Teeth Allen head bolt for mounting stump grinder teeth and pockets. Why hardware matters, inspection tips and how to keep a cutter wheel tight.
tagline: Allen head mounting bolt for Greenteeth stump grinder teeth and pockets.
summary: This Green Teeth Allen head bolt is replacement mounting hardware for the Greenteeth stump grinder tooth system. Teeth and pockets are only as secure as the bolts that hold them, so fresh hardware is a key part of keeping a cutter wheel safe and running smoothly.
highlights: Allen head bolt for Greenteeth tooth systems
Replacement hardware for teeth and pockets
Socket head design for use with a hex key or bit
Worth replacing when bolts are worn, stretched or damaged
Use with matching nuts and torque specs
specs: Mounting teeth and pockets to the cutter wheel
Match to your tooth series and wheel

p: Green teeth stump grinder systems are popular because they let you replace individual teeth and pockets instead of a whole wheel. That design depends on the hardware. Every tooth and pocket is held on by bolts that take a beating with every pass through roots, rocks and dirt.

Worn or stretched bolts can let teeth loosen and shift. A loose tooth cuts poorly, wears out its pocket faster and can break or be thrown from the wheel. Keeping fresh, correct hardware on the wheel is one of the most important parts of stump grinder maintenance.

Searches for green teeth usually come from operators looking for teeth, pockets or hardware for their wheel. Whatever part you are buying, confirm the series and the position on the wheel before ordering, since teeth, pockets and bolts are not always shared across series.

An Allen head bolt uses a hex socket in the head, tightened with a hex key or bit instead of a wrench on the outside of the head. On some cutter wheels, that socket head design makes it easier to reach and tighten the hardware in tight spaces between pockets.

Over time, the hex socket can fill with dirt or wear from repeated use. Clean the socket before inserting the key so it seats fully. If a socket is rounded out or damaged, replace the bolt instead of trying to make it work. A stripped head becomes a much bigger problem the next time you need to change a tooth.

Check the wheel at the start of each day and during long grinding jobs. Look for missing, cracked or worn teeth, worn pockets, and bolts that are loose, bent or worn. Use the tooth pattern and torque specifications from Greenteeth or your grinder manufacturer when you replace parts.

Many operators replace hardware whenever they replace teeth or pockets. It costs little and prevents most loose-tooth problems. Make sure the nuts you use match the bolts and are the type the system calls for.

Keep a small kit on the grinder or the truck: spare bolts, nuts, the correct hex key or bit and a torque wrench. A wheel can lose a tooth to a hidden rock at any time, and having hardware on hand keeps you working.

Before you work on the cutter wheel, shut the engine off, remove the key and wait for the wheel to stop completely. Wear gloves and eye protection; teeth are sharp and debris collects around the wheel. When grinding, keep everyone well back from the debris zone, and follow your machine's operator manual. See more stump grinding teeth, pockets and hardware, including the 700 Series straight pocket.

faq.q: What are Green Teeth?
faq.a: Greenteeth is a stump grinder tooth system made by Green Manufacturing. It uses replaceable teeth, pockets and hardware on the cutter wheel.

faq.q: Why use an Allen head bolt?
faq.a: The hex socket head can be easier to reach and tighten on some cutter wheels. Use the hardware type your tooth system and wheel call for.

faq.q: How often should I replace tooth bolts?
faq.a: Replace any bolt that is loose, bent, stretched or has a damaged head. Many operators replace hardware each time they change teeth or pockets.

Worn teeth show rounded or chipped carbide, and the grinder slows down and throws dust instead of chips. Some teeth can be rotated to use a fresh edge. When the carbide is gone or cracked, replace the tooth.
Buying teeth for a stump grinder in sets makes sense for busy crews, since it lets you replace a full row or the whole wheel at once and keep cutting even.

name: Corona 22 in Steel Leaf Rake with 48 in Wood Handle
title: Corona Leaf Rake, 22 in Steel Head, 48 in Handle
h1: Corona Leaf Rake: 22 in Steel Head, 48 in Wood Handle
meta: Corona leaf rake with a 22 in steel head and 48 in wood handle, built for tree job cleanup, leaves and fine debris. Uses, care tips and who it is for.
tagline: A sturdy steel leaf rake for cleaning up after tree work and landscaping.
summary: This Corona leaf rake pairs a 22-inch steel head with a 48-inch wood handle for cleaning up leaves, twigs, sawdust and chip spill on tree and landscape jobs. Steel tines hold up better than plastic when you are raking through gravel, mulch and small sticks.
highlights: 22 in steel head for wide, efficient strokes
48 in wood handle with a familiar, solid feel
Steel tines handle twigs and mixed debris
Good for lawns, beds and gravel edges
A simple, durable tool for every cleanup crew

body.h: The cleanup tool every truck needs
p: Tree work leaves a mess. Even after the chipper has eaten the brush and the blower has cleared the driveway, there are always twigs in the lawn, leaves in the beds and small chips around the stump. A good rake is still the fastest way to get that last layer of debris into a pile or onto a tarp. That is the job this Corona leaf rake is built for.

The 22-inch head is wide enough to cover ground quickly without being so wide that it catches on every shrub and edge. The steel tines flex enough to rake leaves cleanly but stay stiff enough to pull twigs and small sticks out of the grass.

On removals, a common routine is to rake the lawn into windrows, then pull the windrows onto a tarp and drag it to the chipper or the dump trailer. A wide steel rake makes that routine quick, and it does not mind the occasional chunk of bark or small branch in the pile.

Plastic and poly rakes are light and gentle on lawns, but they wear quickly when you rake through gravel, rough mulch or the mixed debris that comes off a tree job. Their tines can snap in cold weather. A steel head is more durable and keeps its shape longer, which makes it the better choice for crews that rake every day.
The trade-off is that a steel rake can be a little harder on delicate turf and a bit heavier. For most crew cleanup work, that durability is worth it.

The 48-inch wood handle gives a comfortable, traditional feel. Wood absorbs some vibration and does not get as cold as metal in winter. Keep the handle out of standing water and store the rake under cover so the wood stays sound. A light sanding and a wipe of linseed oil every season will keep the handle smooth and help prevent splinters.
Check the connection between the head and the handle from time to time. If it loosens, tighten or repair it before the head comes off in the middle of a job.
Hang the rake by the handle or store it head-up when you are done. Leaving it tines-down on the truck bed bends tines over time, and a rake with bent tines skips over debris instead of collecting it.

This rake suits tree crews, landscapers, groundskeepers and homeowners who want a durable, simple tool for leaves and light debris. Pair it with a backpack blower like the Husqvarna 580BTS for big cleanups, and use it to finish the edges, beds and corners the blower misses. Browse more landscaper tools for the rest of the cleanup kit.
Wear gloves when raking debris from tree work. Small splinters, thorns and sharp twig ends are common, and gloves make a long cleanup much more comfortable.

faq.a: The head is 22 in wide, with steel tines.

faq.q: What is the handle made of?
faq.a: It has a 48 in wood handle.

faq.q: Is a steel rake good for lawns?
faq.a: Yes, for leaves and twigs. It is more durable than plastic for mixed debris, though plastic rakes are a little gentler on delicate turf.

summary: The Husqvarna backpack sprayer uses an 18V battery-powered pump and a 4-gallon tank, so you get steady spray pressure without pumping a handle all day. It suits plant health care, landscape maintenance and property work where you cover a lot of ground with a wand.
highlights: 18V battery-powered pump, no hand pumping
4-gallon tank for longer runs between refills
Steady pressure for even coverage
Backpack design with shoulder straps
Suited to plant health care and landscape spraying
specs: Liquid applications for landscape and plant health

p: Manual backpack sprayers work, but they ask a lot. One hand pumps while the other aims the wand, and pressure rises and falls with every stroke. A battery-powered pump changes that. Pull the trigger and the pump keeps pressure steady, so coverage is more even and your arm is free to focus on aiming.

That matters on plant health jobs where you treat multiple beds, shrubs or small trees on a property. A backpack sprayer 4 gallon in size holds enough to make real progress before you need to refill, while still being light enough to carry once it is full.

It also helps with consistency. Steady pressure means a more consistent droplet size and application rate, which matters when you are following a label rate or calibrating a sprayer for a specific product.

Arborists and landscapers use backpack sprayers for a range of applications: foliar fertilizers, horticultural oils, herbicide spot treatments around landscape beds, and other liquid products labeled for the target plant and pest. The 4-gallon tank and backpack design make it practical for walking a property and treating plants as you go.

Clean the tank, pump and wand thoroughly after every use, especially when switching products. Residue from an herbicide can damage the next plant you spray. Triple-rinse according to the product label and dispose of rinse water properly.

Calibrate before you start a job. Spray a measured area with plain water, time it and check how much you used. That tells you how to mix and how fast to walk so you apply the rate on the label. Recheck calibration when you change nozzles or products.

The pesticide label is the law. Read and follow it for every product you mix and apply, including the personal protective equipment it requires, mixing rates, re-entry intervals and environmental restrictions. Many states require a pesticide applicator license for commercial application. Check your state's rules before you treat customers' trees and landscapes.

Wear the PPE the label calls for, which often includes chemical-resistant gloves, eye protection and long sleeves. Avoid spraying in windy conditions, and keep sprays away from water, pollinators and non-target plants. Store products and the sprayer securely away from children and pets.

body.h: Battery care and who it is for
p: Charge the battery before each job and store it in a cool, dry place. Do not leave it in a hot truck cab for long periods. Check your battery and charger compatibility before you buy, since the sprayer needs a compatible 18V pack.

The Husqvarna 4 gallon backpack sprayer suits plant health technicians, landscapers and property owners who spray regularly and want to stop hand pumping. Browse more landscaper tools for the rest of your maintenance kit.

faq.a: It holds 4 gallons.

faq.q: Does it need to be pumped by hand?
faq.a: No. An 18V battery runs the pump, so you get steady pressure without hand pumping.

faq.q: Do I need a license to spray for customers?
faq.a: Many states require a pesticide applicator license for commercial application. Check your state's requirements and always follow the product label.

name: Husqvarna Trim Force Square Trimmer Line
title: Husqvarna Trim Force Square Trim Line
h1: Husqvarna Trim Force Square Trim Line
meta: Husqvarna Trim Force square trim line for string trimmers. Why a square profile cuts cleaner, how to pick a diameter and how to load and store line.
tagline: Square-profile string trimmer line for clean cuts in grass and weeds.
summary: Husqvarna Trim Force square trim line is a square-profile string trimmer line made for cutting through grass and weeds cleanly. The square edges bite into stems better than round line, which helps on thick growth along fences, beds and tree bases.
highlights: Square profile with cutting edges
Cleaner cuts in thick grass and weeds
Fits trimmer heads that accept the matching diameter
Good for edging around beds, fences and hardscape
Husqvarna line for Husqvarna and other trimmers
specs: String trimmers and brushcutters with line heads
Match to your trimmer head (see listing)

p: Round trimmer line is durable and cheap, but it tends to smash and tear grass rather than slice it. Square trim line has four edges that act like small blades as the head spins. The result is a cleaner cut, especially in tough weeds and thick grass, and a neater finish along edges.

For tree crews and landscapers, that matters around the base of trees, along fence lines and in overgrown corners where round line struggles. Square line can wear a little faster on concrete and stone edges, so pick the right line for the job.
Many landscape crews keep both on the truck: square line for lawns and overgrown areas, round line for heavy edging along hardscape. Matching the line to the job saves time and line.

Husqvarna string trimmer line comes in different diameters, and the right one depends on your trimmer head and engine. Thicker line cuts heavier growth and lasts longer, but it needs more power to spin. Too thick a line on a small trimmer makes the engine bog and wears out the clutch.
Check your trimmer head or operator's manual for the recommended diameter range. If you run a mix of light and heavy trimmers, keep a spool of each size on the truck and label them.

Buying line in larger spools saves money for crews that trim every day, while smaller packs make sense for homeowners. Either way, the same rules apply: the right diameter for your head, wound neatly and stored properly.

Wind line evenly onto the spool in the direction marked on the head, keeping it tight and not crossing the two sides on dual-line heads. Leave the right length out of the eyelets and trim excess before starting. Uneven winding causes line to jam and stop feeding.

Store trimmer line out of direct sun and away from heat. Line that dries out becomes brittle and breaks more easily. Some users soak line in water before loading to help keep it flexible. Keep spools in a sealed bag or bin to stop them drying out over the season.
If your trimmer has a bump-feed head, keep the bump knob and eyelets clean and replace worn eyelets. Worn eyelets cut line and cause it to break off short.

Wear eye protection, hearing protection and long pants. Trimmers throw debris hard and fast. Keep bystanders and pets well back, and be careful around tree trunks: repeated trimmer contact damages bark and can seriously injure young trees. A mulch ring around tree bases cuts down on trimming close to the trunk.

faq.q: Is square trim line better than round?
faq.a: Square line usually cuts cleaner in thick grass and weeds. Round line can be more durable along concrete and stone edges.

faq.q: What diameter trim line do I need?
faq.a: Check your trimmer head or manual. Use the diameter range it recommends for your engine and head.

faq.q: Will Husqvarna trim line fit other trimmers?
faq.a: Usually, as long as the diameter matches what your trimmer head accepts.

name: Jail Brake Lowering Device
title: Jail Brake Lowering Device: Jailbreak Rigging Device
h1: Jail Brake Lowering Device (Jailbreak Rigging Device)
meta: Jail Brake lowering device, the jailbreak rigging device for controlled lowering in tree removals. How friction lowering works and safe rigging tips.
tagline: Tree-mounted friction device for controlled lowering on rigging jobs.
summary: The Jail Brake lowering device, often searched as the jailbreak rigging device, is a friction device that mounts to the tree to control the lowering line on removals. It lets the ground crew add or remove friction to lower heavy pieces smoothly instead of relying on wraps around the trunk.
highlights: Friction lowering device for tree rigging
Mounts to the tree to control the lowering line
Helps the ground crew lower heavy pieces smoothly
Reduces wear on the trunk compared with wraps around the stem
For trained rigging crews only
specs: Controlled lowering in removals and rigging
Use the rope types and sizes the manufacturer specifies

p: When you rig a piece out of a tree, the energy of that piece has to go somewhere. The rigging block or natural crotch redirects the line, and the lowering device at the base turns that energy into heat through friction. The ground worker controls how much friction is applied and lets the piece down at a controlled speed.

Without a lowering device, crews take wraps around the trunk. That works on light pieces, but it is hard to control on heavy ones, it damages bark and it is difficult to adjust mid-lower. A dedicated device like the Jail Brake gives the ground crew a consistent, adjustable friction point.

body.h: How it fits into a rigging system
p: A typical system has a rigging point aloft, often a block on a sling, a rigging line tied to the piece, and the lowering device mounted to the tree at the base. The ground worker manages the tail of the line through the device. More wraps or more friction slow the piece; fewer let it run faster.

Search terms like jailbreak lowering device usually come from crews comparing it to other friction devices such as port-a-wrap style tools and bollards. The idea is the same: give the ground worker control. Fit, mounting and rope compatibility vary by device, so follow the manufacturer's instructions.

Mounting matters. The device needs to be attached securely at a height and position that lets the ground worker stand clear of the drop zone, keep a good grip on the tail and see the piece coming down. Plan the setup before the climber makes the first cut, not after.

Rigging forces can be much higher than the weight of the piece, especially when a piece is allowed to free-fall before the line catches it. Every component in the system, including the lowering device, slings, blocks, rope and the tree itself, must be rated for the loads and in good condition. Do not exceed the device's rated working load.

Rigging should only be planned and performed by trained crews following ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions. Inspect the device before every use for cracks, deformation, grooving and wear. Keep the ground crew out of the drop zone and use clear communication between the climber and the person on the lowering device.

The Jail Brake suits removal crews that rig regularly and want a dedicated friction device at the base. Pair it with a good rigging block, rigging slings and a rigging line that are all rated for the loads you plan to put on them. Browse more lowering devices to compare options.

If you are new to rigging with a mounted friction device, start with light pieces, practice with the full crew and build up gradually. Learn how many wraps or how much friction a given piece needs before you take on big wood.

faq.q: What is the jailbreak rigging device used for?
faq.a: It is a friction lowering device mounted to the tree that lets the ground crew control the speed of rigged pieces during removals.

faq.q: How is it different from taking wraps on the trunk?
faq.a: A lowering device gives more consistent, adjustable friction and avoids damaging bark, especially with heavier pieces.

faq.q: Who should use a lowering device?
faq.a: Trained rigging crews following ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions. Rigging forces can be very high.

name: DMM Hitch Climber Pulley
title: DMM Hitch Climber Pulley for Arborist Climbing
meta: DMM Hitch Climber pulley for arborist friction hitch systems. How it tends the hitch, how to set it up, and inspection and safety notes for climbers.
tagline: A climber pulley built to tend a friction hitch on a doubled-rope system.
summary: The DMM Hitch Climber pulley is a climber pulley designed to sit below a friction hitch and tend it as you advance. It became one of the standard pieces in arborist moving-rope systems because it makes slack tending smoother and the hitch easier to manage.
highlights: Designed to tend friction hitches in moving-rope systems
Attachment points for hitch, carabiner and hitch cord
Smooth sheave for easy slack tending
Keeps the hitch aligned and the bridge connection clean
A long-standing standard in arborist climbing kits
specs: Multiple attachment holes for hitch and carabiner
Arborist climbing ropes, check DMM's diameter range

p: In a moving-rope system, the climber advances by pulling slack through a friction hitch. The hitch climber pulley sits right below the hitch on the rope. As you pull the rope's tail, the pulley pushes the hitch up, so the system tends slack smoothly without you having to reach up and manage the hitch by hand.

That is why it caught on. Before pulleys like this, climbers often tended hitches by hand or used a simple ring setup. The Hitch Climber made climbing smoother and faster and kept the hitch dressed and aligned through the day.

It also helps keep the friction hitch from rolling or getting pulled out of shape, which makes descents more predictable. Many climbers find that their hitch grips and releases more consistently with a hitch-tending pulley in place.

The pulley has multiple attachment holes. A typical setup attaches the friction hitch cord and the bridge carabiner through the pulley, with the rope running over the sheave. Exact setups vary, and the friction hitch you use, such as a Distel or VT, affects how the system behaves.

Learn the setup from a qualified trainer and follow DMM's instructions. A small mistake in how the hitch cord is attached or how the carabiner is loaded can turn a reliable system into a dangerous one. Practice on the ground at low height before you climb with a new system.

The DMM hitch climber pulley is popular because it is well made and easy to use, but it is not the only option. Some climbers prefer different pulley shapes, swivels or lighter designs. Whatever you choose, make sure it is rated for life support, compatible with your rope diameter and designed for the way you climb.

If you are just starting to use a hitch climber, buy a complete system that has been tested together: rope, hitch cord, pulley and carabiners. Compatibility between parts matters more than any single component.
Weight, sheave size and how the pulley sits on your bridge all affect how a system feels. Try a few setups with a trainer or experienced climber before settling on one.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standards, be used according to the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every use. Only trained climbers should use it.

Inspect the pulley before every climb: check the side plates for cracks, burrs or deformation, make sure the sheave spins freely, and look for grooving where the rope runs. Retire it if it has been dropped from height onto a hard surface, shows damage or does not run smoothly. Browse more micro pulleys to compare options.

faq.q: What is a hitch climber pulley?
faq.a: It is a pulley that sits below the friction hitch in a moving-rope system and pushes the hitch up as you pull slack, making climbing smoother.

faq.q: Can I use any friction hitch with it?
faq.a: Common arborist hitches such as the Distel and VT are often used. Follow DMM's instructions and get training on the setup you use.

faq.q: How do I inspect the DMM Hitch Climber?
faq.a: Check for cracks, burrs, deformation and grooving, and make sure the sheave spins freely. Retire it if it is damaged or has been dropped onto a hard surface from height.

Wraps around a range of stem and limb sizes
Protects bark and rope compared with a bare-rope tie-in
Works with SRT and moving-rope systems when used as instructed
Easy to pack in a climbing kit

See the manufacturer's markings and instructions

p: Tying in directly around a limb works, but it puts friction on the bark and the rope and does not always give you the best rope angle. Canopy anchors give a clean, consistent anchor point. They spread the load around the stem, protect the tree and reduce rope wear.

A soft canopy anchor uses a textile sling or cord instead of a metal anchor. That makes it lighter and quieter in the kit bag, and it conforms well to irregular stems. Many climbers prefer textile around the tree for that reason.

Canopy anchors are especially common with SRT, where the rope is fixed in the tree and the climber ascends with mechanical devices. A good anchor makes it easier to set a reliable tie-in and to choose the best spot for the work you plan to do.

In single rope technique, the canopy anchor is where your rope is fixed in the tree. In moving-rope systems, it can provide a friction-saving redirect at the tie-in point. The details depend on the anchor's design, your system and the manufacturer's instructions.

Whatever system you use, think about the forces at the anchor. In SRT, the full load goes onto a single anchor point and the limb or stem must be strong enough. Inspect the tree carefully, choose a sound, well-attached stem and avoid dead or weak wood.

If you are setting a canopy anchor for SRT, consider whether the tie-in point allows a good work position for the whole job, or whether you will need to re-anchor partway through. Thinking it through from the ground saves time and reduces unnecessary changeovers aloft.

Look at the anchor's length and how it fits the stem sizes you usually climb on, the hardware it uses, whether it can be set and retrieved from the ground and whether it is rated for life support. Some climbers keep two anchors of different lengths for different trees.
Make sure every connection is compatible: rope, carabiners, rings and the anchor itself. A canopy anchor is only as strong as the weakest link in the system.
Practice setting and retrieving your anchor on the ground before you rely on it in the tree. Know how it should look when properly set, so you can spot a problem from below.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standards, be used according to the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every use. Only trained climbers should use it. Textiles wear faster than metal, so inspect the anchor for cuts, abrasion, glazing, chemical contamination and UV damage before every climb. Retire it if you have any doubt.
Keep textiles away from chainsaw fuel, bar oil and sharp tools. Store them dry and out of sunlight. Browse more climbing gear to complete your kit.

faq.q: What are canopy anchors used for?
faq.a: They create a secure tie-in point around a stem or limb in the canopy, protecting the tree and rope and giving a consistent anchor.

faq.q: Is a soft canopy anchor safe for SRT?
faq.a: It can be when it is rated for life support, used according to the manufacturer's instructions and set on a sound stem. Get training in SRT anchoring first.

faq.q: How often should I inspect a textile anchor?
faq.a: Before every climb. Look for cuts, abrasion, glazing, contamination and UV damage, and retire it if in doubt.
